text:
tariq.m: Hey all, first-day CI question. My pipeline for `redwood/metrics-ingest` runs a step that posts test annotations using the GitHub Checks API and it's failing with a 403 from the checks endpoint. I'm new so not sure which token to ask for.

buildkite-bot: Build #12 failed - step: annotate-tests (exit code: 1)
```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/metrics-ingest/check-runs -> 403 Forbidden
Error: POST .../check-runs: 403 Forbidden - resource does not have required scope: checks:write
```

devex-ryan: Welcome! That error usually means the token used by the pipeline doesn't have the "checks: write" permission or the Buildkite GitHub App isn't granted Checks permissions for the repo. Which auth method is the step using (pipeline secret vs app)?

tariq.m: The step runs `./scripts/annotate-tests --github-token=$CHECKS_TOKEN`. I don't see CHECKS_TOKEN in the pipeline env. Thought Buildkite app would cover it.

infra-maya: For creating check runs you either need a PAT with the `checks:write` scope (or `repo` which includes it) or the GitHub App must have "Checks: Read & write" permission. Our org used to have the app permission toggled off for Checks by default.

ci-oncall-bot: Onboarding note: avoid creating personal long-lived PATs. Request a scoped CI bot token via #eng-infra or ask infra to enable Checks permission for the Buildkite App on the repo.

emma.s: If it's your first run from a forked PR, note GH masks secrets and some app actions are blocked. For org branches the app can act if installed with the right permissions.

devex-ryan: Quick unblock: I'll add a short-lived masked SECRET_CHECKS_TOKEN (scoped checks:write, repo) to the pipeline so you can finish validating your PR. Long-term we prefer enabling the Buildkite App Checks permission or moving annotations into the `check-annotator` service account.

infra-maya: I checked the app install page - Buildkite installed for "Some repos" and Checks permission currently set to "Read only". To grant write we'd need an org admin to approve. If you want immediate access I'll drop a temporary token into the pipeline.

tariq.m: Thanks, Ryan. Appreciate the quick help.

devex-ryan: Added SECRET_CHECKS_TOKEN (masked) to the pipeline. Re-run the failed job when ready. Also adding a preflight in our annotation step to error with a friendly message if the token or app permission is missing.

tariq.m: Re-ran  annotate-tests now posts annotations and the check-run created with status completed. Logs show HTTP 201 Created. :tada:

infra-maya: Follow-ups: (1) eng-infra to update onboarding checklist to call out Checks permissions and the `check-annotator` service account. (2) Request org admin to flip Buildkite App Checks from Read to Read & write for repos that use annotations. (3) Add pipeline preflight to detect missing CHECKS_TOKEN and print actionable guidance.

ci-oncall-bot: Build #12 (re-run) passed - step: annotate-tests :white_check_mark:

tariq.m: Great, thanks everyone and glad that saved my first PR panic. Will PR a small note to onboarding docs about where I got stuck.
